samples.title: Round desk: Proof strip
samples.statement:
Inputs
`readings` is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless task 1 says otherwise.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `finishTimes`. Each number in `readings` is the work time needed by a job. All jobs are ready at time 0, in input order. The worker gives the first job up to `k` time units. If it still needs work, put it at the back of the line. Then serve the next job. Record when each job finishes, measured from time 0. Record these finish times in original job order. A job needing 0 time finishes at time 0 and uses no worker time.
2. Complete `roundDeskProofStrip` so it returns `finishTimes`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `readings` is [1, 7, 3, 4, 3] and `k` is 3, then `finishTimes` is [1, 18, 7, 17, 13] and `roundDeskProofStrip` returns [1, 18, 7, 17, 13].

Rules
- If `finishTimes` is empty, return [].
- `k` (a whole number from 1 to 8) is the most time units a job gets in one turn.

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `readings` is [8, 4, 0, 3, 4] and `k` is 7.
TEST DATA 2: `readings` is [4, 4, 8, 4] and `k` is 7.

samples.title: Round desk: Peak ticket
samples.statement:
Inputs
`readings` is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless task 1 says otherwise.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `finishTimes`. Each number in `readings` is the work time needed by a job. All jobs are ready at time 0, in input order. The worker gives the first job up to `k` time units. If it still needs work, put it at the back of the line. Then serve the next job. Record when each job finishes, measured from time 0. Record these finish times in original job order. A job needing 0 time finishes at time 0 and uses no worker time.
2. Find the largest number in `finishTimes`. Store it in `largest`.
3. Complete `roundDeskPeakTicket` so it returns `largest`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `readings` is [4, 5, 4, 6, 6] and `k` is 4, then `finishTimes` is [4, 21, 12, 23, 25] and `roundDeskPeakTicket` returns 25.

Rules
- If `finishTimes` is empty, return 0.
- `k` (a whole number from 1 to 8) is the most time units a job gets in one turn.

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `readings` is [13, 8, 11, 13, 0] and `k` is 3.
TEST DATA 2: `readings` is [8, 9, 9, 9] and `k` is 1.

samples.title: Round desk: Boss receipt
samples.statement:
Inputs
`readings` is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless task 1 says otherwise.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `finishTimes`. Each number in `readings` is the work time needed by a job. All jobs are ready at time 0, in input order. The worker gives the first job up to `k` time units. If it still needs work, put it at the back of the line. Then serve the next job. Record when each job finishes, measured from time 0. Record these finish times in original job order. A job needing 0 time finishes at time 0 and uses no worker time.
2. Multiply each number in `finishTimes` by its position, counting from 1: the first number by 1, the second by 2, and so on.
3. Add those products. Store the sum in `weightedTotal`.
4. Complete `roundDeskBossReceipt` so it returns `weightedTotal`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `readings` is [9, 6, 5, 5, 6] and `k` is 4, then `finishTimes` is [31, 26, 27, 28, 30] and `roundDeskBossReceipt` returns 426.

Rules
- If `finishTimes` is empty, return 0.
- `k` (a whole number from 1 to 8) is the most time units a job gets in one turn.

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `readings` is [0, 17, 9, 17, 6] and `k` is 7.
TEST DATA 2: `readings` is [8, 8, 8, 1] and `k` is 5.
